Hi Samantha / Marissa —

Thanks for looping me in. Below are concise talk tracks and ROI bullets you can use when framing the ask to Alex and procurement/security. I'll run the 28 Apr enablement and tailor slides to the audience.

Suggested champion talk tracks (one-liners):
- "Redwood gives us predictable latency and isolation with Dedicated pools — so we can meet peak SLAs without overprovisioning."
- "We can pilot Redwood Dedicated for a narrow set of endpoints and measure cost/performance vs current setup in 6 weeks."
- "Redwood's observability gives per-route token cost and latency breakdowns so we can quickly identify regressions."

ROI / TCO bullets (for Alex):
- Estimated token cost reduction: 30–45% vs current managed endpoints (depends on batch/cache usage).
- Expected latency improvement: median p95 reduced from ~420ms to ~180–250ms in Dedicated for our observed workloads.
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, limited to 5 top customer-facing prompts; success criteria tied to latency p95 and cost per 1M tokens.

Procurement / security quick answers to likely questions:
- SOC 2: provided in SOC2-pack.pdf; we can schedule a 30m call with our security lead for any technical Qs.
- Network: Dedicated can sit in your VPC via Private option; we'll provide a network diagram and guide.
- Data handling: default retention policy and KMS options documented in the technical overview.

Suggested next steps for the 28 Apr enablement:
1) 10m — framing & success criteria (Samantha + Alex).
2) 15m — security/procurement Q&A (Marissa + Rishi).
3) 10m — immediate pilot scope and runbook.

I'll prepare 6–7 slides (1-page ROI, 2 slides technical, 2 slides runbook + acceptance criteria, 1 slide risks/mitigations).

See you on Tue 28 — I will share slides by EOD Mon 27.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
